subcategory: memory-augmented, self-guided routing across multiple unlabeled corpora
problem: RAG systems assume a static, well-organised corpus with fixed retrieval logic, whereas real environments contain many heterogeneous, unlabeled sources and the system must learn which source to query.
architecture: SegMem-RAG: a Segment Planner (inspired by event segmentation theory) splits reasoning into localised decision segments (source selection, subquery); a Feedback Evaluator self-assesses each retrieval outcome in natural language; a Memory Controller keeps procedural, semantic and episodic symbolic memory of source utility; a cold-start explorer probes unfamiliar corpora. No retraining or supervision.
retriever: multilingual-e5-large per-corpus indexes, top-5 knowledge and memory entries
knowledge_source: pool of heterogeneous corpora (BEIR collections, MedRAG corpora, OmniEval, DBpedia, legal corpora, Wikipedia)
key_results: Open-domain average token F1 47.5 vs 45.8 for EnumRAG (retrieve from all corpora) and 42.1 for DRAFT.
Financial QA average fact-level F1 34.1 vs 32.5 for DRAFT; BioASQ 44.0 vs 42.0 for Reflexion.
Random corpus selection (BlindRAG) averages only 15.7 on open-domain QA.
strengths: Addresses a realistic multi-source setting where sources are unlabeled and imbalanced.
Learns from experience without supervision; compared against oracle corpus-selection strategies.

limitations.text: Up to 32 reasoning segments per query imply many LLM calls; cost and latency are not reported in the main results.
Evaluation on 500 sampled questions per dataset with a 7B reasoning model; financial and biomedical scores rely on an LLM judge.

title: SegMem-RAG: Adaptive Memory for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Open-Ended Knowledge Environments
